messages:
elaine: heads-up — CI nsys runs on gpu-1 started failing this morning, seeing CUPTI errors and empty kernel timelines. started when we rolled the image yesterday.

elaine: command we run: `nsys profile --output /tmp/trace --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=cpu -- python3 -u tests/trace_smoke.py`

elaine: error snippet from runner: `CUPTI ERROR: cuptiActivityEnable failed (CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED)` and nsys summary: `No activity captured` (but process definitely touched the GPU).

mike: which driver / CUDA / nsys versions on the new image?

elaine: image: rwinf/gpu-base:2026-03-10, nvidia-driver 535.86, CUDA 12.2, nsys 2024.1. The old image (2026-02-28) had driver 525.x and nsys 2023.4 and traces were fine.

ravi: sounds like a CUPTI ABI mismatch. nsys bundles its own cupti libs sometimes and the driver/CUDA combo can break that. Can you paste ldd of the nsys-runner process or `ldd $(which nsys)`?

elaine: pasted below (truncated):
```
ldd /opt/nvidia/nsight-systems/2024.1/bin/nsys
  libcupti.so => /usr/local/cuda-12.2/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so
  libcudart.so.12 => /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcudart.so.12
```

sarah: two quick possibilities: 1) perf_event/perf permissions (nsys uses perf APIs for hardware counters and some CUPTI integration), 2) CUPTI init failing because of mismatched lib paths.

mike: also check /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid — our runner images set it to 2 by default which blocks some perf ops. lowering to 1 or 0 often fixes capture.

elaine: tried `sysctl kernel.perf_event_paranoid=1` in a debug run and got a different error: `cuptiActivityEnable failed: CUPTI_ERROR_USER_ABORT` then nsys hung.

ravi: odd. Another known quirk: newer drivers introduced stricter CUPTI permission checks when container seccomp or missing capabilities (SYS_PTRACE) are used. CI containers run with reduced caps. Try running the container with `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE --cap-add SYS_ADMIN` or `--privileged` just to confirm it's a cap issue.

elaine: ran with `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE` — CUPTI init succeeded, trace captured, kernels show up. But we can't keep CI privileged.

sarah: ok that confirms a capability restriction. Workarounds: a) adjust runner to add minimal caps for profiling-only jobs, b) use a non-instrumented smoke that collects nvtx only (no perf), c) upgrade/downgrade nsys/CUPTI so it falls back to a capture path that doesn't need ptrace.

mike: FYI, NVidia release notes mention a bug in driver 535.86 where CUPTI fails when seccomp blocks ptrace-style calls. It was fixed in 535.101. We should either pin image to a driver with the fix or add an image variant for profiling.

elaine: good catch. For the immediate regression I'm going to: 1) add a flaky guard to the failing CI job, 2) add a special profiling job image with `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE` so perf traces continue to work, 3) file an infra ticket to evaluate bumping driver to 535.101.

ravi: also log to NVIDIA: include full `nsys --version`, `nvidia-smi -q`, and a minimal reproducer that fails without caps. They ask for CUPTI env dumps too: `LD_PRELOAD`, `CUPTI_LIB` paths.

elaine: done — filed infra ticket RW-4678 and opened nvidia support case with logs (case 2026-0312-NSYS).

sarah: one more perf note for runtime folks: the missing traces hid a batching/KV-cache hotspot — we couldn't see the tiny memcpy kernels that indicate KV cache warmup. When we re-ran with caps, those memcpy kernels are visible and point to a 30ms stall in KV loads on large-batch paths.

elaine: copying that to perf board — we likely need to change our kernel selection heuristic: consider prefetching KV for predicted next sequences and reduce large-batch eagerness for cold cache.

mike: actionable: (a) infra: profiling image + driver bump plan, (b) runtime: reproduce locally using the profiling image and capture full timeline (memcopy, kernel launch latencies), (c) perf: add a small NVTX-marked test to catch KV warmup regressions.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline note — profiling-image build triggered: #build-3321 (profiling-variant).

elaine: thanks — I'll run the repro on the profiling image and post the timeline screenshot here once I have it. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks all. If anyone needs the quick reproduction script: `scripts/repro/nsys_cupti_check.sh` (on the repo root). It toggles perf_event_paranoid and runs a tiny Llama-style KV cache fill that exhibits the bug.

mike: leaving a reminder to update our docs (devex runbook) with the minimal caps + driver matrix for nsys captures so future people don't waste time. :memo:

elaine: filed runbook PR: #512 — adds driver matrix and CI profiling job notes.

ravi: awesome, will follow up on the NVidia case.

elaine: closing the loop here once I paste the timeline and the KV-cache kernel screenshots.
